findings.evidence: Identical `rcases hr with ⟨i, j, h⟩ | ⟨i, j, h⟩` at lines 149, 173, 244; `PresentedGroup.toGroup`/`toGroup.of` exist at mathlib/Mathlib/GroupTheory/PresentedGroup.lean:135,139.
findings.fix: Prove the general result once: `def lift {G} [Group G] (f : Fin (n-1) → G) (hcomm : ∀ i j, i.1+2 ≤ j.1 → f i * f j = f j * f i) (hbraid : ∀ i j, i.1+1 = j.1 → f i * f j * f i = f j * f i * f j) : BraidGroup n →* G := PresentedGroup.toGroup (by rintro _ (⟨i,j,h⟩|⟨i,j,h⟩) <;> simp [...]) ` with `@[simp] lift_sigma`. Then `exponentSum`, `permHom`, `castSuccHom` are each one call supplying only the two group-level identities, and `exponentSum_rel`/`permHom_rel`/`castSucc_rel` disappear.
findings.issue: No `BraidGroup.lift` universal property. `exponentSum_rel` (149), `permHom_rel` (173) and `castSucc_rel` (244) each repeat `rcases hr with ⟨i, j, h⟩ | ⟨i, j, h⟩` plus the same `commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm` / `mul_inv_eq_one` boilerplate (175/190, 246/251, and again at 110/122). Any downstream map out of B_n (Burau, Temperley-Lieb, closure maps in the roadmap) must unfold `artinRelations` and repeat it a fourth time.

findings.evidence: Line 101 `theorem comm (i j : Fin (n - 1)) (h : i.1 + 2 ≤ j.1)` vs. line 23 `$\sigma_i \sigma_j = \sigma_j \sigma_i$ whenever $|i - j| \ge 2$`.
findings.fix: State the main lemma with the symmetric hypothesis `(h : i.1 + 2 ≤ j.1 ∨ j.1 + 2 ≤ i.1)` (or `2 ≤ max i.1 j.1 - min i.1 j.1`), deriving both directions from `ArtinRelation.comm`; keep the ordered form only if needed as a private step.
findings.issue: `comm` is stated only for `i.1 + 2 ≤ j.1`, while the module doc (line 23) states the relation as `|i - j| ≥ 2`. Users holding `j.1 + 2 ≤ i.1` cannot apply it directly and must case-split and `symm` by hand; `rw [comm]` fails on half of the intended instances.

findings.evidence: castSucc_rel lines 245-254 discharge the two relations via `comm`/`braid_rel` with index bounds from `omega`; the only use of the target size is `hi : i.1 < n` at 247/252, which `m ≤ n` supplies equally.
findings.fix: Define `BraidGroup.map (h : m ≤ n) : BraidGroup m →* BraidGroup n` (generators `fun i ↦ sigma ⟨i.1, by omega⟩`, relations discharged by `comm`/`braid_rel` exactly as now) and set `castSuccHom n := map (Nat.le_succ n)`, with `map_sigma` replacing `castSuccHom_sigma`.
findings.issue: `castSuccHom` is proved only for `n → n + 1`, but the proof uses nothing about `n + 1` beyond `i.1 < n - 1 → i.1 < (n+1) - 1`; the identical argument gives the standard inclusion `BraidGroup m →* BraidGroup n` for `m ≤ n`, of which the successor case is one instance.

findings.evidence: `FreeGroup.Lift.aux` is the internal helper used to build `FreeGroup.lift` (mathlib/Mathlib/GroupTheory/FreeGroup/Basic.lean:665,680); `PresentedGroup.mk : FreeGroup α →* PresentedGroup rels` at mathlib/Mathlib/GroupTheory/PresentedGroup.lean:47.
findings.fix: Define `evalWord w := PresentedGroup.mk (artinRelations n) (FreeGroup.mk w)` (or `FreeGroup.lift sigma (FreeGroup.mk w)`); then `evalWord_nil`/`evalWord_append` are `map_one`/`map_mul` composed with `FreeGroup.mul_mk`, and no braid-specific list induction is needed.
findings.issue: `evalWord` is a bare-function special case of the general free-group lift: `FreeGroup.Lift.aux sigma w = FreeGroup.lift sigma (FreeGroup.mk w) = PresentedGroup.mk _ (FreeGroup.mk w)`. Because it is not a homomorphism, `evalWord_append` (139) has to be reproved at the braid level instead of following from `map_mul`.

summary: The braid group is defined without its universal property, so each of the three homomorphisms out of B_n re-destructures `artinRelations` and re-proves the same two relation checks; `comm` is also stated only in the ordered form despite the module doc advertising |i-j| ≥ 2.
